Add a cycle, such as a daily rhythm, that drives a model's latent processes

Source: R/ctModelPeriodicComponent.R
ctModelPeriodicComponent.Rd

Adds a pair of latents, <name>_cos and <name>_sin, that rotate with a fixed period and have no noise of their own (DRIFT[cos, sin] = -2 pi / period and DRIFT[sin, cos] = 2 pi / period), so they follow the cosine and sine of the time of day, or of whatever the period is. Each latent in indices is driven by both, through estimated effects DRIFT[k, <name>_cos] and DRIFT[k, <name>_sin], which set the amplitude and phase of the cycle's effect. Each driven process responds with its own dynamics, so a fast process follows the cycle closely and a slow one smooths and delays it.

Usage

ctModelPeriodicComponent(
  ctm,
  period,
  indices = seq_len(ctm$n.latent),
  name = "cycle",
  individual = TRUE
)

Arguments

ctm

A model from ctModel(type = 'ct').

period

The cycle's period, in the data's time units: 24 for a daily rhythm with time in hours.

indices

Which latents the cycle drives, by position.

name

Prefix for the added latents, predictors and parameters.

individual

Let each subject's cycle deviate from the clock.

Value

The extended model.

Details

The cycle is set to the clock at each subject's first observation, using two time independent predictors, <name>_cos0 and <name>_sin0, the cosine and sine of that time over the period, which ctPeriodicPhases adds to the data. The time variable must therefore count from an origin shared by all subjects, such as hours since midnight of a common day. With individual = TRUE each subject's cycle may also be shifted from the clock and differ in strength, through an initial deviation of the pair with an estimated standard deviation. This allows rhythms that differ between people, or a time origin that is not shared.

The effects start at zero.

Needs the julia backend.

See also

ctPeriodicPhases for the predictors it uses, ctFitAdequacy's periodic family, which detects cycles a model is missing, and ctModelImprove, which adds a cycle where that family finds one.

Examples

m <- ctModel(type = 'ct', manifestNames = c('Y1', 'Y2'),
  latentNames = c('eta1', 'eta2'), LAMBDA = diag(2))
m2 <- ctModelPeriodicComponent(m, period = 24)
m2$latentNames
m2$TIpredNames
p <- m2$pars
p[p$matrix %in% 'DRIFT' & (p$row > 2 | p$col > 2) &
  (!is.na(p$param) | p$value != 0), c('matrix', 'row', 'col', 'param', 'value')]
